title: The Walk to the Far Beach

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A teen asks to camp two nights at the far beach with a friend: say yes with a few conditions, or ask them to wait a little.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and (teen), a friend, want to walk to the far beach on the other side of the island and camp there for two nights. It's a famous walk. Lots of grown-ups have done it. (subject) has thought of everything: food, water, a fire-starter, which paths to take. (subject.He/she) is now standing in front of (friend) with the expression of someone who has already decided what the answer will be.

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

choices.label: Say Yes, with a Few Conditions

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (friend) asks some questions. Which way? What if it rains? When will they be back? (subject) has an answer for almost all of them, and the ones (subject.he/she) doesn't, (subject.he/she) works out. They agree on a time to be home. Two days later (subject) comes back sunburnt, exhausted, triumphant, and an hour early, which (subject.he/she) mentions several times.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: "Not this time," says (friend). "The weather's turning. When the storms have passed, yes." (subject) is furious and says so. (friend) doesn't change (friend.his/her) mind, but doesn't pretend it's an easy answer either. That night a storm rolls in and rain hammers on the roof. (subject) says nothing about it. Neither does (friend). They go when the weather clears.
